title: 残るコロナの後遺症　中東緊迫、雇用助成の積立金まだ回復1割
extracted_text:
連合の芳野友子会長は4月24日、赤沢亮正経済産業相に面会した際に要請書を手渡した。中東情勢の悪化に伴い企業が雇用を守るための支援策を状況に応じて検討するよう求めた。この要請書には企業の生々しい声が書かれている。

「必要なポリエチレンが手に入らない。このままだと生産を止めなければならない」（繊維素材）、「断熱材の価格改定（40%上昇）やトルエンの出荷停止で防水工事の遅延発生」（建設・建材）、「塗料不足により4月から生産調整中」（車体製造）――。

石油由来の製品や原材料の供給の目詰まりや偏りが長期化すれば実体経済への影響が大きくなる。芳野氏は面会後、記者団に「まだ休業にいたった企業はないが、もし操業停止すると雇用調整助成金（雇調金）の活用が必要になる」と指摘した。

労働基準法では企業が工場の稼働を止めるなどして従業員を休ませた場合、手当を支払わなければならない。休業手当と呼び、平均賃金の6割以上の額を支払う。大企業の場合、その費用の最大半分を厚生労働省が助成する。これが雇調金だ。

雇用保険料のうち企業のみが支払う料率0.35%分を財源とする。平時に積み立てておき、有事に取り崩している。

新型コロナウイルス禍の後遺症が残るいまの財政は脆弱だ。コロナ前の2019年度は雇調金の積立金は1.5兆円を確保していた。20〜22年度の累計で支給額は6.4兆円に及び、すぐに枯渇した。

資金不足は政府の一般会計から1.3兆円を繰り入れ、さらに失業給付の原資になる別の積立金から2.9兆円を借り入れることで工面した。失業給付の積立金からの借り入れは1兆円棒引きする措置を講じたものの、返済額は24年度末で1.4兆円残る。

「財政はまだひどい状態だ。10年かけて返済する途上にある」と厚労省幹部は話す。いまは保険料の収支は年2000億円規模の黒字が見込まれ、積み立てと返済の双方に回している。24年度末時点の雇調金の積立金は1442億円とコロナ前の19年度の1割しかない。

08年のリーマン・ショック後に雇調金支給額は09年度で6000億円規模、10年度で3000億円規模だった。この幹部はいまの積立金が枯渇する可能性はまだ低いが、最悪のシナリオに陥れば「再び借り入れるなどファイナンスを考えないといけない」と打ち明ける。

厚労省は先んじて手を打ちにくい。高市早苗首相は4月27日、燃油などの節約要請について「経済・社会活動を今止めるべきではない」と語り、慎重な考えを示した。

厚労省は悩ましい立場だ。雇調金の資金問題を正面から持ち出せば、雇用への不安や経済危機が迫っていると社会に捉えられかねない。現時点ではショックが大きくなる恐れや兆しがないか、注視するにとどめている。
translated_text: Tokyo Confederation of Trade Unions (JFTU) President Yoshino Tomoko met with Economy, Trade and Industry Minister Akasawa Ryusei on April 24 and submitted a petition requesting that support measures be considered as needed to help companies preserve jobs amid the deteriorating Middle East situation. The petition contains candid voices from businesses. "We can't get the polyethylene we need. If this continues, we'll have to stop production," one textile materials company wrote. "Insulation material price adjustments (40% increase) and toluene shipping stoppages are causing delays in waterproofing construction," reported a construction and building materials firm. "Due to paint shortages, we've been adjusting production since April," said an automotive manufacturer." If supply bottlenecks and imbalances for petroleum-derived products and raw materials continue for an extended period, the impact on the real economy will be significant. After the meeting, Yoshino told reporters, "No companies have fully shut down yet, but if operations stop, the Employment Adjustment Subsidy (EAS) will need to be utilized." Under Japan's Labor Standards Act, when companies suspend factory operations and have employees take leave, they must pay an allowance called "shutdown pay," which must be at least 60% of average wages. For large companies, the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare subsidizes up to half of these costs. This is the EAS. The fund is financed by the 0.35% employment insurance premium rate paid only by employers. It accumulates during normal times and is drawn upon during crises. With the lingering aftereffects of the COVID-19 pandemic, the current fiscal position is fragile. In fiscal 2019 before COVID, the EAS reserve fund stood at 15 trillion yen. From fiscal 2020 to 2022, disbursements totaled 6.4 trillion yen and were quickly depleted. The shortfall was covered by transferring 1.3 trillion yen from the government's general account and borrowing 2.9 trillion yen from another reserve fund used for unemployment benefits. Although measures were taken to reduce 1 trillion yen of the borrowing from the unemployment benefit reserve, 1.4 trillion yen in repayments remained as of the end of fiscal 2024. "The fiscal situation is still in severe shape. We're in the process of repaying over 10 years," a MHLW official said. Currently, premium balance is expected to show an annual surplus of around 200 billion yen, which is allocated to both accumulation and repayment. The EAS reserve fund at the end of fiscal 2024 was 144.2 billion yen, only 10% of the fiscal 2019 pre-COVID level. After the 2008 Lehman Shock, EAS disbursements were around 6 trillion yen in fiscal 2009 and 3 trillion yen in fiscal 2010. The official said the risk of the current reserve being depleted is still low, but in the worst-case scenario, "we'd have to consider financing such as borrowing again." MHLW finds itself in a difficult position. If it openly addresses the EAS funding issues, it could be perceived as signaling growing employment concerns or an imminent economic crisis. For now, it remains watchful for any signs or indicators that shock might intensify. Prime Minister Ishiba stated on April 27 regarding requests for fuel and other savings that "we should not stop economic and social activities right now," showing a cautious stance.
title_en: Lingering COVID Aftereffects: Middle East Tensions Push Employment Subsidy Reserve to Just 10% of Pre-Pandemic Level
